title: Uptake of New Lipid-coated Nanoparticles Containing Falcarindiol by Human Mesenchymal Stem Cells
protocol: Set up a block heater/sample concentrator, desiccator, digital dispensing system with a 1 mL glass syringe, 12 mL glass vial, magnetic stirrer, and magnetic flea (15 mm x 4.5 mm, cylindrical shape with PTFE coating) inside the glass vial.
Dispense 2.4 mL of 250 µM falcarindiol stock dissolved in a 70% EtOH water mixture into a scintillation vial.
Evaporate the liquid fraction using the sample concentrator for approximately 4 hours to obtain dry falcarindiol at room temperature without heat.
Insert the scintillation vial containing dried falcarindiol into the block heater.
Add 16.3 µL of 31.64 mM DSPC chloroform stock solution, clean syringe with chloroform after addition.
Add 3.4 µL of 17.82 mM DSPE PEG 2000 chloroform stock solution, clean syringe with chloroform after addition.
Add 24 µL of 25 mM cholesterol chloroform stock solution, clean syringe with chloroform after addition.
Add 6 µL of 4 mM DiI chloroform stock solution, clean syringe with chloroform after addition.
Wrap the vial containing chloroform stock solutions with aluminum foil to protect DiI from light.
Leave the sample overnight in the desiccator to evaporate the chloroform.

Dissolve the desiccated sample in absolute ethanol to a final volume of 1.2 mL, yielding DSPC, DSPE PEG 2000, cholesterol, and DiI concentrations of 0.43 mM, 0.05 mM, 0.5 mM, and 0.02 mM respectively.
Take the 12 mL glass vial and fill it with 9 mL of purified water.
Add a magnetic flea to the vial containing 9 mL of water.
Place the vial on the magnetic stirrer, stirring at 500 rpm.
Attach the 1 mL glass syringe to the dispensing system.
Clean the syringe with chloroform by pulling it into the glass syringe and manually dispensing into a waste collector at least ten times.
Prime the syringe with ethanol to remove any air bubbles and old solvent.
Aspirate 1 ml of the organic phase using the syringe.
Insert the syringe into the middle of the water in the vial, maintaining it steady.
Inject the solution at a speed of 833 µL/s.
Remove the vial from the stirrer immediately after injection.
Transfer the sample to a 50 mL round-bottom flask (RBF).
Attach the RBF to the rotary evaporator.
Evaporate 1 mL of organic solvent using the rotary evaporator at room temperature.
Avoid excess bubble formation during evaporation.
Transfer the nanoparticle suspension from the RBF to another 12 mL glass vial.
Ensure that the volume transferred is 9 mL.
Split the sample into two 12 mL glass vials (4.5 mL in each).
Add 0.5 mL of ultrapure water to one of the vials.
Add 0.5 mL of 10x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the other vial.
Take out 1 mL of each sample for particle size measurement.
Turn on the DLS instrument and set the desired temperature at 20 °C, until it stabilizes.
Set the instrument parameters as follows: data acquisition time = 4 s, number of acquisitions = 30, auto-attenuation function = On, and the auto-attenuation time limits = 0.
Fill the plastic cuvette with 1 mL of nanoparticle suspension and start the measurement.
Report the measured size depending on the solvent used (water or PBS).
Repeat the measurements 24 h after the synthesis, to check for particle aggregation.
Grow hMSCs in minimum essential medium (MEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin/streptomycin, in a humidified chamber at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Seed approximately 50,000 cells on absolute-EtOH-sterilized #1.5 coverslips in 6-well plates.
Add MEM to achieve a final volume of 3 mL per well.
Incubate for 24 h under the same conditions as specified previously.
Without removing the medium, add 3 µL of nanoparticle solution to reach a final falcarindiol concentration of 5 µM.
Incubate for an additional 24 h in the same conditions.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Fix cells in 4% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature.
Store fixed cells in PBS at 4°C until imaged.
Alternatively, permeabilize fixed cells with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 30 min.
Wash cells twice with PBS after permeabilization.
Stain cells with 250 µL of 300 nM DAPI for 5 minutes in the absence of light.
Use a widefield fluorescence microscope equipped with an electron-multiplied CCD camera to acquire images.
Use the 150x NA 1.45 oil objective and the GFP LP channel for imaging.
Acquire confocal microscopy images using the 63x NA 1.4 oil objective.
Use an Argon laser (514 nm) for DiI acquisition in confocal microscopy.
Use a two-photon laser (780 nm) for DAPI acquisition in confocal microscopy.
Verify the uptake of nanoparticles into cells through confocal microscopy imaging.
